Your questions

NDIS support FAQs for Canberra

These NDIS support FAQs cover starting services and making arrangements with Barmil in Canberra. Find practical answers, then contact us with questions about your own circumstances.

Starting support and making arrangements

For questions about NDIS support in Canberra, begin with service areas, your goals and the arrangements you need. Availability and funding must be discussed for your situation.

Which parts of Canberra do you serve?

Barmil serves Canberra, including Belconnen, Gungahlin, North and South Canberra, Woden Valley, Weston Creek, Tuggeranong and the Molonglo Valley. Tell us your suburb so we can discuss suitable arrangements and availability.

How do I start receiving support?

Call, email or use the enquiry form to tell us about your goals, the support you need and your Canberra suburb. We will discuss suitability, funding arrangements and availability before agreeing on services.

Can I choose the support I receive?

Your goals and preferences guide the discussion. You can ask about one service or a combination, then agree on a support arrangement that is suitable for your needs.

Will my NDIS plan cover these services?

The answer depends on your plan, your disability-related needs and the service being proposed. Check your funding and payment arrangements before agreeing to support.

Can a family member or support coordinator contact you?

Yes. A person you choose can help make the enquiry or join the discussion. We will clarify your preferences and consent before sharing information or making arrangements.

Can I ask about changing providers?

Yes. Tell us the support you are looking for and any timing considerations. Check notice periods and existing service agreements before making a change.

Do you provide overnight or 24-hour care?

These arrangements must be discussed individually. They are not assumed to be included in daily tasks or shared living assistance.

Do you support every NDIS funding arrangement?

Please tell us how your plan is managed. We will confirm whether the proposed service and payment arrangement can be accepted before you start.

Can services change as my needs change?

You can contact us to discuss changes to your goals, routine or support needs. Any changes should be agreed as part of your service arrangements.

Are activities, travel and tickets included in the price?

Ask for a clear explanation of support time, travel and any other costs. Ordinary tickets, memberships and meals are different from the support needed to participate.

What should I include in my first enquiry?

Your name, preferred contact method, Canberra suburb and a brief description of the service you need are a helpful starting point. Avoid sending sensitive records in an initial enquiry.

How do I give feedback?

Call or email Barmil and explain what you would like to discuss. You can involve a support person of your choice and ask about the process for raising a concern.

A practical guide

Understanding NDIS supports in Canberra

Understanding NDIS supports in Canberra starts with what you need help doing. This guide explains the differences between Barmil’s services so you can prepare questions and choose the support to discuss.

Assistance with everyday life

Help with tasks you currently need assistance to complete, such as personal routines or essential household jobs.

  • Personal care
  • Household tasks
  • Daily tasks and shared living

Learning everyday skills

Support to practise a skill over time, rather than simply having a task done for you.

  • Life skills development
  • Life stage and transition support
  • Accommodation and tenancy assistance

Participating in your community

Assistance with taking part in activities you choose. Individual support, group programs and tailored participation have different purposes.

  • Community participation
  • Group activities
  • Innovative community participation

Travelling to what matters

Discuss the journey, your access requirements and any assistance you need at your destination. Confirm what is included before making a booking.

  • Travel and transport assistance

Using this NDIS support guide

If you are comparing support options in Canberra, choose NDIS supports by their purpose. Assistance with a task, learning to do it, attending an activity and joining a group can require different arrangements.

Four things to clarify before starting

  1. Your goal: the routine, task or activity you want help with.
  2. The service: what support is being offered and whether it suits your needs.
  3. The arrangements: timing, availability, location and the people involved.
  4. The costs: support time, travel and any other charges, along with how payment will be managed.

Check your individual funding arrangements.

A service being listed on this website does not mean it is automatically funded for every participant. Your plan and disability-related needs determine which supports may be appropriate. Ask for clarification before agreeing to services.

Accommodation and tenancy assistance is different from supplying SDA housing. Daily tasks in a shared home do not automatically mean a SIL arrangement. These terms describe different types of support.

For current scheme information, visit the official NDIS participant website. For provider registration information, visit the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.

NDIS accommodation & tenancy assistance in Canberra

Barmil provides practical NDIS accommodation and tenancy assistance in Canberra. We help you work through the documents, routines and decisions involved in accessing or maintaining a suitable home.

Talk about your support0449 644 722

Make the next step towards home feel clearer.

Our NDIS accommodation services focus on tenancy assistance, rather than supplying a property. You may want help gathering information for an application, organising household responsibilities or planning the practical steps involved in a move.

We start with your housing goals, access needs and the people you want involved. Together, we identify the information to gather and questions to ask. You remain involved in decisions about your home, and any legal or specialist tenancy advice needs an appropriate adviser.

Help with daily routines after a move

Practical possibilities

What support can involve

Planning your next steps

Clarifying your accommodation goals and the practical tasks involved.

Applications and information

Assistance organising relevant documents and working through application requirements.

Tenancy routines

Support to understand everyday tenancy responsibilities and keep track of important information.

Preparing for change

Help organising the practical steps around a move or a change in living arrangements.

Let’s discuss the right arrangement.

Contact us with a brief description of your current situation and what you would like to change. We will discuss the assistance you need, your funding arrangements and the appropriate next steps.

Tenancy assistance is different from supplying housing or Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA). It does not guarantee a property, pay rent or replace specialist tenancy advice.

We serve Canberra, including Belconnen, Gungahlin, North and South Canberra, Woden Valley, Weston Creek, Tuggeranong and the Molonglo Valley. Explore our service areas.

No housing vacancy or property is being advertised here. This service supports the process of accessing or maintaining accommodation.

No. SDA is a separate type of specially designed housing. Accommodation and tenancy assistance focuses on practical support with accessing and maintaining a home.

Can I get help before I move?

Contact us to discuss the planning, documents and everyday skills you need help with. We will explain what assistance may be suitable for your situation.

NDIS life skills development in Canberra

Barmil supports NDIS life skills development in Canberra through learning and practice. Choose a practical skill you want to build, such as preparing a meal, planning shopping or organising your week, and we can discuss manageable steps.

Talk about your support0449 644 722

Practise today. Build confidence over time.

NDIS life skills support is about learning how to do something and practising it over time. Development of life skills can involve breaking a task into steps, trying a step together and reviewing what makes it easier to remember or repeat.

A useful goal might be writing your own shopping list or preparing one familiar meal. We discuss a suitable setting and pace, then revisit the skill with you. Progress looks different for everyone, and no particular outcome or timetable is promised.

Life skills development focuses on learning. If you mainly need assistance carrying out a routine today, daily living support may be the more relevant service. The two can complement one another without having the same purpose.

Practise expressing needs, asking questions and taking part in daily decisions.

Community routines

Discuss skills for getting ready, navigating familiar activities and participating more independently.

Let’s discuss the right arrangement.

Choose a goal you would like to work towards. We will discuss the steps, the setting in which you want to practise and how support can be reviewed as your confidence changes.

Skill development is different from having a task completed for you. The right mix of assistance and learning depends on your goals, support needs and plan arrangements.

NDIS innovative community participation in Canberra

Barmil’s NDIS innovative community participation in Canberra starts with a particular barrier to taking part. We discuss your circumstances and goals, then explore a tailored approach where a standard activity arrangement may not fit.

Talk about your support0449 644 722

A more individual way to take part.

NDIS innovative community participation focuses on an individual approach to a participation goal. We ask what has made involvement difficult, what you have already tried and which practical changes or preparation might help.

For example, you might want to work through the steps involved in approaching an unfamiliar setting before deciding whether to take part. This is an example to discuss, not a scheduled program or a promise of a particular outcome. Suitability, funding arrangements and available assistance must be confirmed.

This page focuses on tailored preparation and individual barriers. For assistance attending everyday activities, see social and community participation. For shared sessions, see group activities.

Support to attend everyday community activities · Shared group activities

What support can involve

Understanding barriers

Explore the circumstances that make usual participation options difficult.

Reviewing what works

Let’s discuss the right arrangement.

Tell us what you would like to participate in, the barriers you have encountered and any existing support arrangements. We will discuss suitability, the proposed scope and your funding arrangements.

Innovative community participation is not a general promise to fund hobbies or leisure activities. It is distinct from routine community access and standard group programs, and must be suitable for your individual needs.

We serve Canberra, including Belconnen, Gungahlin, North and South Canberra, Woden Valley, Weston Creek, Tuggeranong and the Molonglo Valley. Explore our service areas.

Your questions

How is this different from ordinary community participation?

Ordinary participation support concerns assistance accessing chosen everyday activities. Innovative participation starts with a particular barrier and explores an individually tailored response. We clarify the proposed service with you before you agree.

Is there a set activity program?

The focus is on your circumstances and goals. Contact us to discuss whether an individual approach is appropriate and available.

Will my NDIS plan cover it?

That depends on your plan, the proposed support and your disability-related needs. Funding should be checked before you agree to a service.

In the community · Canberra

NDIS social & community participation in Canberra

Barmil offers NDIS community participation support in Canberra to help you access social activities and places you choose. Tell us who you want to spend time with, where you want to go and the assistance you need to take part.

Talk about your support0449 644 722

More room for the things and people you enjoy.

NDIS social and community participation centres on the activity you want to attend. You might need community access support to visit a local library, meet friends or take part in a cultural event. The choices and interests are yours.

We discuss the practical details: where you want to go, what help you need on arrival and during the activity, and any arrangements for getting home. Support time, travel and ordinary activity costs should be clarified before you book.

Everyday community access is the focus here. A shared session belongs under group activities. Where an individual barrier needs tailored preparation, innovative community participation may be worth discussing.

Group and centre activities · Tailored innovative participation

Practical possibilities

What support can involve

Social connection

Assistance to participate in agreed social activities and maintain connections.

Community access

Discuss support to visit local places or take part in community activities.

Culture and interests

Explore activities that reflect your interests, culture and preferences.

Confidence to participate

Plan practical steps around access, communication and getting comfortable in a setting.

Let’s discuss the right arrangement.

Tell us what you enjoy, what you would like to try and any support or access requirements. We will discuss options, availability and the arrangements needed before an activity goes ahead.

Support to participate and the ordinary cost of an activity are different. Tickets, meals, memberships and transport arrangements should be discussed separately before booking.

We serve Canberra, including Belconnen, Gungahlin, North and South Canberra, Woden Valley, Weston Creek, Tuggeranong and the Molonglo Valley. Explore our service areas.

Your questions

Can I choose the activities?

Your interests guide the conversation. Tell us what you would like to do so we can discuss suitable support and availability.

Is this only for group activities?

No. Community participation concerns support to access activities. Group programs are a separate option with their own arrangements.

Can I start with a familiar place?

Yes. You can ask to discuss support around a familiar setting or routine, then consider other activities at a pace that suits you.
